The derivation begins with the foundational property that monotone unions and intersections preserve Baire sets, establishing closure under countable operations. This allows the definition of λ(E) = ∫v(x⁻¹E ∩ Y)dμ(x), where v is a measurable function and Y is a subgroup. The finiteness of λ(C) for compact Baire sets C ensures λ is a Baire measure. Left invariance follows from the group structure of X, ensuring λ(xE) = λ(E). Uniqueness of λ up to scalar multiple c leads to c = 1 by comparing λ(C) = μ(C) on compact cosets. Thus, λ = μ, confirming Haar measure regularity. Failure modes arise when compactness or invariance fails, breaking the equivalence between λ and μ.
